body.md: What is the SI unit of work?

wrong.hint: QUACK. That one measures a force. Work is force times distance: what unit does that make?
QUACK. That one measures a speed. Work is force times distance: what unit does that make?

saccharine.tip: Work and energy share one unit.
saccharine.key: W = Fd, so the unit is N·m, which is the joule, J.

slip.b: the unit of force, not work
slip.c: the unit of speed, not work

saccharine.narration: Work is force times distance. A newton times a meter is a joule. So work is measured in joules.

body.md: A car goes around a circle at constant speed. Which way does its acceleration point?

wrong.hint: QUACK. The car keeps turning inward. Which way must the push on it point?
QUACK. The circle is flat. Which way does the car keep turning?

saccharine.key: In uniform circular motion a = v^2/r points toward the center (centripetal).

slip.b: the outward 'centrifugal' feel, not the acceleration
slip.c: gravity's direction, not the turning acceleration

saccharine.narration: Centripetal means center seeking. The car keeps turning inward, so its acceleration points toward the center of the circle.

body.md: Which is Newton's law of gravitation?

wrong.hint: QUACK. Move the masses farther apart. Should the pull get stronger or weaker?
QUACK. Bigger G means stronger gravity. Is G on top or on the bottom?

saccharine.key: F = G m1 m2 / r^2: the inverse-square law.

slip.b: r^2 on top: the pull would grow with distance
slip.c: G on the bottom and r not squared

saccharine.narration: Gravity is G times the two masses, divided by the distance squared. Farther apart means a weaker pull.

body.md: A $2\ \text{kg}$ puck moves at $3\ \text{m/s}$. Use $p = mv$. Find its momentum, in $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.

wrong.hint: QUACK. $mv$ means $m$ times $v$. Which operation did you use?
QUACK. $mv$ means $m$ times $v$. Which operation did you use?

saccharine.narration: Momentum is mass times velocity. Two kilograms times three meters per second is six kilogram meters per second.

body.md: A $10\ \text{N}$ push moves a box $4\ \text{m}$ in the direction of the push. Use $W = Fd$. Find the work, in $\text{J}$.

wrong.hint: QUACK. $Fd$ means $F$ times $d$. Which operation did you use?
QUACK. $Fd$ means $F$ times $d$. Which operation did you use?

saccharine.narration: Work is force times distance. Ten newtons times four meters is forty joules.

body.md: A motor does $60\ \text{J}$ of work in $3\ \text{s}$. Use $P = W/t$. Find the power, in $\text{W}$.

wrong.hint: QUACK. $W/t$ means $W$ divided by $t$. Which operation did you use?
QUACK. $W/t$ means $W$ divided by $t$. Which operation did you use?

saccharine.narration: Power is work divided by time. Sixty joules over three seconds is twenty watts.
